blogs.title: The "Commissioner-Only" Rule: Why Private Employees Can't Sue for MPWA Penalties
blogs.description: In *Cohen v. Consilio*, the Eighth Circuit narrowly interpreted Minnesota’s Payment of Wages Act (MPWA), concluding that private employees cannot seek average daily wage penalties under the act. This post examines the court's statutory construction analysis under Minn. Stat. § 181.101, exploring how the Minnesota legislature utilized the express inclusion of penalties only in specific subsections ( §§ 181.13 and 181.14) to signal a legislative intent to limit enforcement to the Commissioner rather than individual litigants.

blogs.title: Mootness vs. Standing: Does Settling Overtime Wages Kill a MFLSA Penalty Claim?
blogs.description: The case marked a significant tension between standing and mootness doctrine when an employee settled his baseline labor claims but sought state-funded penalties. Analyzing this first, we will discuss how the court applied the "voluntary cessation" rule from *Friends of the Earth, Inc.*, determining whether the employer's hard-to-proof and potentially permanent policy change precluded the court from considering the penalty's potential to deter future violations.

blogs.title: The Waiver Trap: How Courts Dismiss Claims That Were Stipulated Away
blogs.description: The Eighth Circuit vacated some claims in *Cohen* because the parties qui slip in agreements. This post analyzes the court's handling of the Wage Theft Act and injunctive relief claims, explaining why various court rules permit dismissal of arguments raised only in late-stage briefings or those that were explicitly waived through stipulation agreements that leave the court with no record of development.
